reason: A keeps the original structure (logo, can, headline, CTA, legal) with clean centred alignment, the teal circle stays a corner accent, and spacing is reasonable. Flaws: the can is small, and the legal text is tiny and sits at the very bottom over the light-blue circle. B has the same tiny legal text, now sitting on the blue circle. B also puts the large teal circle behind the logo, sun and can, so the logo and can lose their clean background. The CTA is crammed right under the headline, and the layout is top-heavy with a dead gap above the legal line. B looks less intentional and less polished.

A reads cleanly left to right (bottle, brand, headline, copy, CTA), circles echo the original, no collisions; only minor flaws: small subcopy/wordmark, bottle nearly touches the top and bottom edges. B has the headline 'fizz' colliding with the overlapping circles at top right, a detached SOLSTICE wordmark, a three-line ragged subcopy, an oversized CTA competing with the headline, and a bottle jammed against the edges.

A drops the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow. Its body copy is oversized and left-aligned, so it competes with the headline. The CTA is a tiny button crammed into the lower left, and the divider and legal text are microscopic and jammed at the right edge. The headline is nearly edge-to-edge, and the layout is unbalanced and chaotic. B keeps the full structure: header with logo, eyebrow, headline, divider, body, a clear CTA, 'Ships late June' and legal text, all centred in the original order. Its flaws are a very dense headline, tiny logo and eyebrow, small legal text, and tight margins at this small size.

A: headline is misaligned with the brand and subhead (about 12px further left), runs almost edge to edge with a tiny right margin, and sits over the beige circle. The CTA is floating and off-axis, pills are detached at the bottom, and the pink circle is stranded in the corner. B: a clean left-aligned stack with brand, two-line headline, subhead, pills and CTA, and a clear hierarchy. Flaws: the headline overlaps the circle edge, the pills are small, the CTA is below the pills, and the right side and bottom are empty, with the pink circle floating.

A has a clear left-to-right flow (brand/headline left, details/badges/CTA centre, product in the circle right) and a readable headline and CTA. Flaws: the missing-asset placeholder overlaps the circle edge, the 'FREE ENTRY' text is cramped, the footer is tiny, and the logo is small. B has a mis-ordered hierarchy: the tagline sits above and apart from the headline, and 'Sessions' crowds the pills. The RSVP CTA is shrunk into a tiny pill in a row with the badges, so it is buried. The 'Reserve a spot' text is tiny, the legal text is cramped, the product is small and cut off at the top right, and the layout looks scattered.

A: the plan cards are tiny and their labels are illegible. The order is wrong (Monthly 6, Family 80, Yearly 48), which breaks the sequence and the highlighted yearly card. The legal text and subcopy are crammed into a narrow right column. B: keeps the original order, with labels and prices readable and the yearly card still highlighted. The headline, CTA and fine print are well spaced. Minor flaws: the subcopy under the headline is small, the headline is tightly packed, and the fine print is tiny.

A: the big teal circle collides with the GLACIER wordmark and the can (sun and right leaf sit on it). The headline-CTA gap is cramped, the fine print is stranded in mid-canvas on top of the blue circle, and there is a large dead zone at the bottom. B: the original's structure survives with a clean centered stack (logo, can, headline, CTA, legal) and generous spacing. The circles are pushed to the corners and don't touch the text. The legal text sits near the edge of the lower circle and is tiny, and the can is slightly small, but only minor polish is needed.

A: bottle is cramped against the top and bottom edges. The headline nearly touches the overlapping circles at the right edge, and the circles muddy into a blob. The three-line body copy is jammed between the headline and the oversized CTA, so the CTA competes with the headline. The logo floats alone at left with no clear alignment. B: a clean centred stack of logo, headline, body and CTA reads well, and the bottle sits on the peach circle as in the original. Flaws: the bottle is tight to the top and bottom edges, the body text and CTA label are small, the green circle at right is dead weight, and there is a large empty gap between the text and that circle.

A keeps the original's centred stack: small header band with logo, eyebrow, 4-line headline, divider, body, CTA, 'Ships late June' and legal text, in a sensible order. Flaws: eyebrow and logo are tiny, legal text is nearly illegible, body copy is small, and the layout is cramped against the edges. B has a tall header band and a 5-line headline that crowd the canvas. Its body copy is left-aligned and larger than the CTA, so it competes with the headline. The CTA is a tiny, buried button squeezed beside the legal text, 'Ships late June' is jammed under it, and the eyebrow is nearly invisible. The mixed alignment and the cramped bottom edge make B clearly broken.

A: clean left-aligned stack (brand, 2-line headline, subline, pills, CTA) with a clear hierarchy and shared left edge. Flaws: the headline overlaps the peach circle (intentional-looking), the CTA sits below the pills and is a bit detached, the right circle is a floating dead decoration, and the bottom is empty. B: the headline runs almost edge to edge with nearly no right margin, and its left edge is misaligned with SOLSTICE and the subline. The subline sits on the circle edge, so the text is split across two backgrounds. The CTA is right-shifted and unaligned, and the pills are pushed below it, so the reading order is jumbled. The decorative circle at the top right is arbitrary.

A: the headline is split over two lines and overlaps the circle; the tagline sits in a narrow column that wraps into five lines; the RSVP button is jammed next to the chips, with tiny cramped text and a crowded cluster at the bottom. The tiny 'RSVP Free' button competes with the chips, the product is tiny at the top right, and the layout is jumbled with no clear reading order. B: a clear left-to-right flow of headline, then details, chips, CTA and product. The headline is dominant, the CTA is larger and clear, and the product is bigger on the circle. Flaws: the missing-asset placeholder is still visible at the bottom right, the footer text is tiny, the chip text is small, and the layout is slightly dense on the right.

A keeps the plan order Monthly/Yearly/Family, with the Yearly card still highlighted and the labels readable. The headline is smallish, the legal text is tiny and cramped, and the layout is dense but coherent. B reorders the cards to Monthly/Family/Yearly, which breaks the sequence and moves the emphasis off the middle. Its cards are tiny with unreadable labels and 'per year' text, and its disclaimer is crammed, though the headline and CTA are strong.

A: headline breaks into an orphan 'fizz' on its own line, and the CTA sits only about 20px under it, so that block is cramped. The green circle runs behind the bag and brand. The bag and headline are large and readable, and the CTA is legible. B: the headline stays on one line with comfortable spacing, and the green circle is clear of the bag. The CTA and 'CITRINE' text are small. There is dead space between the brand and the bag, and the whole layout is a plain stacked copy of the original. Overall B is cleaner, with fewer typography flaws.

A: the headline and CTA are large and clear, and the logo and product group together at the left. But the sale ribbon is tilted and jammed in the bottom-left corner. The product is tiny, the legal text is a cramped, tiny 3-line block under the CTA, and the margins are tight. B: the headline is clear and the legal line sits neatly below it. But the sale ribbon overlaps a large dark circle and a bright orange CTA with a stray dot beside the headline, which looks messy. The product is tiny and cropped inside a circle. The legal text is tiny, and the logo reads as an odd round blob. Both are weak. A keeps the product and logo more legible, so it is slightly less bad.

A: clean single-line headline, centered axis, brand/product/headline/CTA order intact, circles echo the original. Flaws: the bottom half of the canvas is crowded while the top has a big empty gap above the bag, the logo is small, the CTA text is tiny, and the bottom third has dead space. B: the logo, bag and CTA are larger and more legible, and the green circle runs behind the bag in a way that echoes the original. Flaws: the headline wraps to leave 'fizz' as an orphan, the CTA button sits almost touching it with a cramped gap, and the green circle sits right behind the logo and bag, which is slightly busy. A is slightly safer on typography.

A: the red SALE ribbon collides with the product and the circle, and the product is half hidden. The headline is small, and the legal line sits tight under it and runs close to the bottom edge. The logo is stranded inside a dark circle on the far left. B: it reads cleanly left to right, with a larger serif headline and a clear CTA. Its flaws are a tiny product with the logo cramped above it, a tilted ribbon pushed into the bottom-left corner, and a three-line legal block jammed against the CTA at the right edge.

A: clean left-to-right flow (product, headline, sub, sale tag + CTA); product is reasonably large and the logo is intact. Flaws: the logo is tiny, the sale ribbon and CTA are crammed at the right edge with the ribbon nearly touching the canvas edge, the legal text is small, and the sub-copy wraps to a lone 'on June 21.'. B: the headline is huge and bleeds close to the left and bottom edges, and the product is shrunk to a tiny bottle in the top right, which loses the key imagery. The sub-copy is tiny and jammed above the CTA, the CTA is oversized and crowds the right edge and the bottle, and the ribbon floats awkwardly over the middle. The right column is cramped while the left is overbearing, and the layout is unbalanced.

A: the headline fills the square at four lines and dominates, but the subtext sits crammed at the bottom as a ragged three-line block beside the CTA. The two are misaligned, and the subtext, CTA and headline are almost touching, so the bottom feels cramped. The tagline is centred oddly and the CTA is detached from its copy. B: keeps the original stack (headline, subtext, CTA) on one centred axis with clear hierarchy and consistent spacing. Minor flaws: the headline's side margins are tight (about 50px) and the block sits slightly high, leaving more empty space below than above. The CTA is small.

A keeps the original order (eyebrow, headline, body, bottle in circle, CTA) with a clean shared left edge and the circle contained behind the bottle. Flaws: a slightly large gap before the CTA, and the CTA is left-aligned while the bottle is centered. B moves 'WEEKEND ONLY' below the body copy, breaking reading order. Its circle overlaps the headline and text, and the CTA is centered while the text is left-aligned, so the layout looks jumbled.

A: the phone is cropped by the left and top edges and the circle is clipped. The headline is jammed against the top, and there is a big dead band at the bottom left. The badge and CTA sit low and are staggered, with the CTA nearly touching the right edge, so the layout is lopsided and cramped. B: the phone and circle are intact and fully visible, and the headline and subtitle are vertically centred in a clear left-to-right flow. The badge stacks above the CTA with a consistent right margin. Flaws: the headline and subtitle are small, there is a large empty gap between copy and badge/CTA, and the badge is tilted and slightly dominant over the CTA.

A: the headline is large and strong, but a big dead gap sits between the tagline and the details. The details block is pushed to the far left edge and misaligned with the centred header and CTA. The can floats off to the right, and the broken 'missing asset' placeholder is still visible in the corner. B: the content is more tightly grouped, with the original's large circle motif and the details, can and pills held together as a unit. Its flaws are a smaller headline, small pill and legal text, the same visible missing-asset placeholder (floating oddly, not edge-anchored), and a large empty bottom band.

A: the product bottle is shrunk to a tiny sliver in the top-right corner and the hierarchy is wrong. The headline is huge, the logo is oversized, and the bottle is nearly lost. The copy and CTA cluster crammed on the right, the sale ribbon floats mid-canvas disconnected from the product, and the headline sits tight to the bottom-left edge. B: a clean three-zone banner. The bottle is at left at a decent size, the centered headline and subcopy are readable, and the CTA and ribbon are on the right. Flaws: the logo is tiny, the ribbon is small and tilted next to the CTA rather than prominent, the legal line is small, and the right column feels crowded against the edge.

A is a clean, centered stack that keeps the original's hierarchy. But the headline, subline and CTA sit above centre, leaving a large dead orange area below (about 30% of the canvas). The subline runs almost to the side margins (about 50px) and is small against the headline. B fills the square with a big four-line headline and has strong hierarchy. But the subline and CTA are crammed along the bottom, with the subline as a ragged three-line block. The headline-to-subline gap is tight, the bottom margin is thin, and the subline and button are not aligned. The cramped bottom and weak grouping are real flaws, but A's empty bottom and edge-tight subline are about as bad, and B has more impact.

A: the circle is cropped awkwardly and sits behind the headline and body text, and the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow is moved below the body copy, which breaks the reading order. The text block is also cramped against the circle edge, the bottle is detached from the circle, and the CTA is centered while the text is left-aligned. B: it keeps the original order (eyebrow, headline, body, bottle, CTA) with a shared left margin. The circle is a clean backdrop for the bottle and the text sits on plain background. Minor flaws: the CTA is small, there is a big gap between the body copy and the circle, and the CTA is left-aligned while the bottle is centered.

A keeps the original's three-zone left-to-right banner: phone circle at left, headline and subline vertically centred, badge stacked above the CTA at right. Flaws: the headline is modest in size, there is a wide dead gap between text and CTA column, and the badge is jammed against the top margin. B is crowded. The phone circle is clipped at the left edge and the headline sits tight to the top. The badge and CTA sit low in the bottom-right and nearly touch each other and the subline. It leaves empty space at top right and bottom left, and the layout is unbalanced and bottom-heavy. The CTA is oversized relative to the headline.

A is a faithful shrink of the original. The content block is compact with a clear hierarchy, but there is a large empty band at the bottom, the missing-asset placeholder box floats unaligned, the circle crops awkwardly, and the info block and can are slightly off-axis. B uses the height better: the headline stack sits higher and the can is bigger and better balanced with the info block. However, the gap between subtitle and date is a dead zone, the left margin is inconsistent with the centred headline, the CTA is stranded low, and the same placeholder box sits bottom-right. Text and pills are small in both. B is marginally better on balance and the circle stays out of the way.

A reads cleanly left to right: phone, SOLSTICE over a one-line headline and subline, two stacked badges, then a clearly separated dark CTA at the right edge. Flaws: the CTA is jammed against the right edge, there is a large dead gap between the text and the badges, the badges are close to equal in weight to the CTA, and the phone is tiny. B squeezes everything into a cramped cluster. The SOLSTICE brand label is crowded against the headline and is not aligned with it. The CTA is stacked directly under the badges with almost no gutter, so it competes with them. The headline wraps to two lines at a small size, there is a big empty gap between the phone and the text, and the phone is cropped close to the top and bottom edges.

A has a clear top-to-bottom flow: left-aligned eyebrow, headline, subline, a product centered in its circle, then CTA and legal. Flaws: the CTA is detached from its copy, the gap above the legal text is large, and the product is small. B puts the circle behind the headline, so '20% off' and 'WEEKEND ONLY' sit on the purple edge, which is a collision. The CTA is jammed under the subline, the legal text is oversized and nearly touches the right edge, margins are inconsistent, and the large dead gap around the product looks unbalanced.

A keeps the bottle as a clear hero, with a readable headline and CTA, and has no collisions. Flaws: the headline and buttons are left-offset and don't share an axis, the NEW badge and CTA are not aligned to each other, there is a dead gap below the bottle, and the decorative circle floats in the corner. B shrinks the bottle into a tiny corner circle that overlaps the translucent circle and touches the top and left edges. Its oversized headline dominates, the NEW and Try It pills are stacked off to the right and cramped, and a large empty area sits bottom-left. The product is lost and the layout is unbalanced.

A: on the 728x90 banner, the 'Cucumber Mint is back' headline is wrapped onto two lines and nearly touches the top and bottom edges. 'SOLSTICE' is tiny. The phone is a thin sliver. The two pills are stacked, with the CTA bulky and dark and about the same weight as the headline, so the elements are crammed into the middle with dead space at the left and right. B: it reads left to right as phone, brand, headline, tagline, badges, then a CTA that stands out at the right. The headline is on one line, bigger and clearly dominant, and the margins are even. Flaws: the tagline and 'SOLSTICE' are tiny, the badge text is very small, the badges are stacked tightly, and the phone is small and its circle is clipped at the edge. It is still clearly better than A.

A: the purple circle collides with the "WEEKEND ONLY" and "20% off" text, so the headline sits partly on the circle edge. The headline is oversized, the CTA is jammed directly under the copy, and a large gap leaves the product floating. The footer text is nearly as big as the body copy and crowds the bottom edge. B: clean left-aligned column with a clear hierarchy (eyebrow, headline, subline), and the bottle sits on its circle as in the original. Flaws: the CTA is detached from the copy by a large gap, the fine print is tiny, and there is dead space at the bottom. The headline is modest for the tall canvas, but nothing collides.

A: the bottle circle is jammed in the top-left corner, cropped by the canvas edge and overlapped by a ghost circle. The headline is left-aligned while NEW and Try It are right-aligned, so there are two competing axes. The NEW badge and CTA are stacked at the bottom right with a big dead area at the bottom left, and the NEW pill is nearly as large as the CTA. B: the bottle is large and centred, which gives a clear hero, and the headline sits below it with the badge and CTA in a row. Flaws: the headline is left-offset and not centred under the bottle, and the NEW pill and CTA row is not aligned to the headline edges. The headline is small relative to the bottle, and the CTA is not dominant. The decorative circle floats randomly top-left. The whole layout is shifted off-centre.
